context.goal: Replace the paper maintenance log for a 22-turbine onshore wind farm with a tablet app that technicians use on the turbine.
context.audience: Technicians, the site manager, the HSE officer and the asset owner's engineer, who will answer the list.

items.meaning: Open a job on a WTG from the tablet; types: scheduled service, fault, inspection, retrofit.
The LOTO checklist is completed and signed by 2 technicians before a job can go to in progress, no exceptions.
Nacelle work logs the climb, the harness check and the second person on the ground.
Parts used are scanned by barcode from the container inventory, with a warning below minimum stock.
Time per job per technician is recorded for OEM warranty claims.
Before and after photos attach to the job, at most 10, compressed on the tablet.
The job report is a PDF in the OEM template so warranty claims are accepted.
A fault job links to the SCADA alarm that triggered it by alarm id.
The app works without signal in the nacelle and syncs at the base.
The site manager sees open jobs by WTG and by technician, with overdue scheduled services marked in a configurable colour.
HSE gets a monthly export of all LOTO records and near misses.
Near miss report: what, where, photo, from any technician; anonymous to the site, visible to HSE.
The app shows SCADA wind speed and blocks opening a nacelle job above 15 m/s.
Retrofit jobs carry the OEM bulletin number.

must_not_invent: a 12 m/s limit for nacelle work (corrected to 15)
overdue jobs shown in red (corrected to configurable)
spare parts ordering from the OEM
notes: Context spec (decision 0011). Glossary terms WTG, LOTO, SCADA, nacelle, HSE and OEM stay as written; "turbine" for WTG is accepted only in addition, never instead. The corrections at the bottom override the list: 15 m/s, configurable colour, anonymous to the site but visible to HSE. G06-07 is flagged ambiguous because the template is missing. The 12 m/s rotor limit is not an item; it is an explanation.
